findings.evidence: dom-1440.json meta viewport 'width=1440'; at 375 the desktop layout is scaled and overflows (sweep ROB-003), so phone users get ~4x-smaller text.
findings.after: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> plus a stacked layout under ~768px

findings.evidence: focus.json: all seven stops use the UA default 'auto 1px' outline with no offset; on the #e63946 primary button a 1px dark ring is barely distinguishable (the sweep flagged only 'WATCH DEMO').
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.7 Focus Visible and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast.

findings.evidence: dom-1440.json: the chips are <div>s with no role or tabindex, yet styled as a selected toggle ('30D' red); they look operable but cannot be reached by keyboard. Nav links all have href '#'.
findings.after: Real <button aria-pressed> controls if interactive, or mark the whole mock aria-hidden="true" and remove control styling
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.1.1 Keyboard and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 2.4.4 Link Purpose for href='#'.

findings.where: mock bar chart highlight and alert severities
findings.evidence: Red vs grey bars and red 'High'/'Med' vs grey 'Low' carry meaning by hue; the dark mock's grey labels (#444 on #111, ~1.9:1, sweep-verified) are unreadable.
findings.after: Severity also by text weight or icon; mock labels >= #9a9a9a on #111
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color and 1.4.3 Contrast.

findings.evidence: No <main> or <header>; the decorative mock's 30+ text nodes (KPIs, months, alerts) are read as content after the h1.
findings.after: <main> around the hero; aria-hidden="true" or role="img" + aria-label on div.hero-right

strengths: Headline and CTA text are large and high-contrast on the light half.
not_investigated: Sweep's 1.00:1 contrast hit on the red '3x' is a measurement artefact (sampling the glyph itself); the numeral is visibly red on white, about 4.2:1, which passes the 3:1 large-text bar. disputed: sampled the text's own fill.
No live keyboard test of 'WATCH DEMO'.
